input.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: Agents and Infra Revenue increased $15.1 billion or 25%. • Azure revenue increased $10.8 billion or 48% driven by demand for services across the platform with continued growth across all workloads.

input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud revenue growth in Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended September 30, 2026) was driven primarily by Azure and other cloud services. This is an interpretive claim about the driver of revenue growth.

Evidence E1 is from the 10-Q filed 2026-10-28 for the period ended 2026-09-30, which is the exact quarter in question. It shows that "Agents and Infra Revenue increased $15.1 billion or 25%" and specifically states "Azure revenue increased $10.8 billion or 48% driven by demand for services across the platform with continued growth across all workloads."

Since Azure contributed $10.8 billion out of the total $15.1 billion increase in the Intelligent Cloud segment (which appears to be referred to as "Agents and Infra" in this filing), this represents approximately 72% of the segment's revenue growth. This clearly supports the claim that Azure and other cloud services were the primary driver of Intelligent Cloud revenue growth.

The claim is purely interpretive/qualitative about what drove the growth, with no specific numeric assertions to verify.
